escalation_rules.statement: Customer Success owns the ongoing relationship with a customer after go-live: renewal, expansion, health monitoring, and executive escalations.
Owns retention and expansion revenue targets, is the final internal escalation point for at-risk accounts before executive involvement (see PROC-CS-001).
Manages one squad (6–9 engineers), owns delivery timelines and is the escalation point for P1/P2 defects assigned to their squad.
escalation point for Implementation Consultants on integration questions involving NexConnect.
Handles the most complex cases, works directly with Engineering on suspected product defects (see PROC-ENG-002, Bug Reporting & Escalation).
escalation point for P1 incidents outside business hours.
Technical Support handles customer-reported issues (tickets) after go-live, following a tiered escalation model.
Deeper product troubleshooting, configuration-level fixes, escalation point for L1.
Level 1 — CSM-handled: Standard account concerns (usage questions, minor dissatisfaction) handled directly by the assigned Customer Success Manager.
Level 3 — Executive (CEO/CTO): Reserved for strategic accounts, contract-value accounts above €100,000 ARR, or reputational-risk situations (e.g., public complaint, data exposure incident).
Define how at-risk or unhappy customer situations are escalated internally.

Level 2 — VP Customer Success: Escalate when: a customer explicitly threatens churn, requests a call with Nexora leadership, or an unresolved P1 incident has affected the account for more than 24 hours.

A technical P1 incident (PROC-SUP-002) affecting a customer does not automatically trigger a Level 2 customer escalation — the CSM makes that judgment based on customer relationship context and incident duration.
escalation_rules.section: Customer Escalation Policy > Relationship to Incident Management

escalation_rules.statement: overdue invoices (30+ days) trigger an automatic reminder, then escalation to the account's Customer Success Manager at 45 days.
escalation_rules.section: Invoice and Payment Process > Customer Invoicing (Accounts Receivable)

escalation_rules.statement: Billing disputes are logged by the AP/AR Specialist and routed to the Finance Manager

escalation_rules.section: Invoice and Payment Process > Dispute Handling

escalation_rules.statement: Any suspected data exposure must be reported to the CISO within 24 hours of discovery, regardless of confirmed severity (see PROC-SUP-002).
Leads unactioned after 3 business days are automatically re-queued and flagged to the Sales Manager.
no formal escalation path exists.
escalation_rules.section: Proposal and Quotation Process > Known Gap

escalation_rules.statement: Unresolved or complex issues escalate to L2, then L3 if a product defect is suspected.
Via monitoring alert (DevOps), Support ticket escalation, or direct customer report.
Any incident with suspected unauthorized data access must be escalated immediately to the CISO, in parallel with standard incident response — see PROC-IT-002.
escalation_rules.section: Incident Management Process > Escalation to Security
